c.tagline: A volcanic lakeside crossroads on the Rwandan border, living in the shadow of Mount Nyiragongo and an active regional conflict.

rides: None (no established ride-hailing apps; moto-taxis and shared taxi-vans only)

taxi.fareNote: There is no metered taxi fleet; fares for shared 'taxi-bus' minivans and moto-taxi ('moto') rides are agreed before departure, often quoted in a mix of Congolese francs and US dollars.

emergency.police: No functioning nationwide emergency number; contact the nearest PNC (Police Nationale Congolaise) post directly
emergency.medical: No ambulance dispatch line; go directly to a hospital (e.g., HEAL Africa, Charité Maternelle) or arrange transport in advance
emergency.note: DR Congo has no reliable 911/112-style emergency system, and in Goma response capacity is minimal. The city has been intermittently under M23 rebel control since January 2025 as part of the wider eastern DRC conflict, and sits roughly 13-18 km from the active Mount Nyiragongo volcano, which erupted destructively as recently as 2021. Travelers should coordinate safety and evacuation planning through their embassy or an NGO/UN security network rather than relying on local emergency services.

avoid.reason: Most governments advise against all travel to Goma and North Kivu — the city was seized by M23 in early 2025 and remains volatile; avoid all road travel outside the city and any crowds or checkpoints.
Carjacking, robbery and extortion at checkpoints occur even in calm periods — move with trusted local contacts, avoid going out after dark, and be very careful with cameras near officials.

hood_desc: The diplomatic and NGO quarter along the Lake Kivu shorefront, home to the Goma Serena Hotel and most embassies/UN offices; the most secure and orderly part of town for visitors.
A lakeside residential neighborhood with a public beach and several guesthouses, popular with aid workers and longer-term visitors wanting lake access.
A dense, central commercial district around Katindo Market with shops, banks, and budget hotels; the practical hub for everyday errands.
A quieter, greener area near the crater lake Lac Vert (Green Lake) and the foothills toward Mount Mikeno; appeals to those wanting distance from downtown noise.
A crowded, informal market district that is the commercial heart for most residents; authentic but chaotic, with basic budget lodging.

water.note: Drink only bottled or properly treated water; supply and quality are unreliable.

transit.hours: No fixed schedules; informal transport generally runs roughly 6:00 AM to 8-9:00 PM and tapers off after dark for security reasons.
transit.pay: Cash only (Congolese francs or US dollars), paid directly to the driver; moto fares are negotiated per trip.
transit.note: Goma has no formal public transit system, no metro, and no fixed-route buses; getting around relies on shared minibuses, moto-taxis, and private/NGO vehicles, with movement sometimes restricted during periods of insecurity.

air: Goma International Airport (GOM) - service has been severely disrupted since the M23 offensive began in January 2025, with only intermittent commercial flights resuming through 2026
bus: Intercity trucks/buses toward Bukavu and other North Kivu towns, subject to security conditions
ferry: Passenger and cargo boats on Lake Kivu to Bukavu and other lakeshore towns

transit.m: Taxi or moto-taxi to city center

tip.r: Tipping is not customary; rounding up or a small token for good service at hotels and restaurants catering to expats/NGOs is appreciated but optional.
